children: The country's second-largest public sector lender, Punjab National Bank (PNB), expects its credit card and cash management services verticals to generate around  ₹200 crore each in quarterly profit from the next financial year as it steps up its focus on digital businesses to boost fee-based income.

The bank has created dedicated digital platforms for three key businesses —  credit cards, supply chain management and cash management services —  each headed by a general manager to drive growth, PNB Managing Director and CEO Ashok Chandra told PTI in an interview.
The initiatives are aimed at strengthening the bank's non-interest income amid anticipated challenges in treasury earnings and loan recoveries, he said.

Chandra said PNB's credit card business, which started in 2008, had a base of around 6.04 lakh cards till March 2025. Following the rollout of its digital platform, the bank added another 5 lakh cards over the subsequent nine months, taking the total base to around 11 lakh.

title: PNB aims for ₹200 crore quarterly profit from credit card, cash management segments
